model: Earnings-based cost-of-equity FCFE DCF (bank-like lender; engine route, retention = NI growth / ROE, net debt zero)

historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs restated on total revenues net of interest expense (FY2022 $52,862m, FY2025 $72,229m from the 10-Ks on file; FY2020 $36,087m from the FY2020 10-K, which is not in the local Extracted set). The prior 6.5% / 13.5% were computed on the XBRL contract-revenue subset. 5yr figures (revenue 14.9%, EPS 32.5%) are inflated by the FY2020 COVID trough -- 3yr (FY2022-FY2025) is the cleaner read: revenue 11.0%, net income 13.0%, EPS 16.0% (buyback-boosted), equity 10.6%. FCF CAGR is not computed: owner FCF is not meaningful for a lender (see inputs.notes).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5yr EPS CAGR 32.5% vs equity 5yr 7.8% diverges far beyond 30% -- an artefact of the FY2020 trough base plus buybacks shrinking equity; 3yr equity 10.6% vs revenue 11.0% is aligned. Selected rate stays the 3yr equity CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands at ~9.8% revenue growth and ~$11.9bn underlying net income on nine months of actuals; growth then decelerates toward ~5% as the Platinum refresh and premium mix-shift tailwinds mature; net margin drifts up from 15.0% to 15.4% as card fees outgrow discount revenue; ROE fades from ~33% toward a still-high 26%; 70-80% of net income is distributed; discounted at a 10.5% cost of equity. Only FY2026 changed in this update.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY2026 closes at the top of what nine months of actuals allow (~10.2% revenue growth, ~$12.1bn underlying net income); card-fee acceleration then sustains a double-digit revenue path via premium mix-shift and Millennial/Gen-Z account growth; margin expands on operating leverage; ROE stays near 33-34%; cost of equity 9.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 is largely banked (~9.3% revenue growth, ~$11.5bn underlying net income with provisions starting to build in Q4); from FY2027 consumer discretionary and travel spend slow to mid-single-digit growth and credit normalises off today's benign levels (30+ day delinquency 1.2%, net write-off rate 2.1% in Q3-2026), compressing net margin from ~14.6% toward ~12.4%; ROE falls toward 20%; cost of equity 12.0%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Earnings-based FCFE-at-cost-of-equity model for a card issuer/network with material on-balance-sheet lending -- not an owner-FCF WACC DCF. Net income is the flow; FCFE = NI less the retention needed to fund balance-sheet/capital growth at the assumed ROE (modeled via the engine's capex_pct_path, same mechanic as NAB.AX); discounted at cost of equity; net_debt held at zero because deposits/debt fund the loan receivables book, not leverage against the network/fee business. See inputs.notes for the full routing rationale and folder precedent (NAB.AX, SOFI, SRBK, IAG.AX).
key_risks_to_valuation: Consumer credit-cycle turn: delinquency and write-offs are benign (1.2% / 2.1% in Q3-2026) and Q3 provisions were flattered by a model-driven reserve release; AXP's premium-skew book is not immune to a harder landing
Card-fee growth deceleration if the Platinum refresh tailwind fades faster than guided; cards-in-force growth has already flattened (proprietary cards 87.6m -> 87.5m in Q3-2026)
Quality of the FY2026 print: Q3 EPS included +$0.74/share of net one-offs (GBTG gain less restructuring) plus discrete tax benefits; this model strips the former into a one-time bridge item
Multiple de-rating could continue rather than stabilise
Bolt-on M&A (TheFork, Swisscard buy-in) diverting capital from buybacks; Q3 buybacks slowed to $1.6bn from $2.3bn in Q2
Regulatory/interchange risk to discount revenue is not separately modelled
Stub convention: FY2026 flow is counted in full and discounted a full year from a November valuation date (net conservative by ~4%, see inputs.notes)

equity_bridge.item: GBTG stake sale gain net of the restructuring charge it funded (after tax)
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q MD&A (AXP_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:2338): gain $982m pre-tax / $751m after tax ($1.11/sh) less restructuring $336m / $253m after tax ($0.37/sh). One-off, already earned, proceeds received after 30 Sep 2026; kept OUT of the Y1 margin so it is not capitalised into later years or the exit multiple. CET1 rose 10.4% -> 10.9% in the quarter, so it is distributable capital, not a regulatory top-up.

bridge.item: Methodology: revenue base rebased from the XBRL contract-revenue subset ($41,304m) to total revenues net of interest expense ($72,229m), margin and retention paths rescaled
bridge.note: value-neutral by construction; the rebased drivers rebuild all three prior scenario values to the cent

bridge.item: Anchor refresh: fully diluted shares 679.0m -> 671.6m (15 Oct 2026 cover count + dilution)

Driver change: FY2026 re-judged on nine months of actuals in all three scenarios (base growth 10.0% -> 9.8%, net margin 14.93% -> 15.0%; bull growth 11.5% -> 10.2%; bear growth 6.0% -> 9.3%, margin 13.72% -> 14.6%), retention for FY2026-27 recomputed
bridge.note: bear +1.88, base -0.27, bull -3.03: the scenario range narrows because most of FY2026 is now known

bridge.item: Anchor refresh: one-off GBTG gain net of restructuring, $498m after tax, added through equity_bridge

bridge.note: no effect on intrinsic value; discount to price is little changed

reconciliation.unchanged: Deliberately left alone: growth, net-margin and retention paths for years 3-10 in every scenario (years 2 growth and margin too; only year-2 retention was recomputed mechanically); cost of equity 10.5 / 9.5 / 12.0; terminal growth 3.0 / 3.5 / 2.0; terminal cap multiples 16 / 19 / 12; weights 25/50/25; hurdle 15%; net debt zero; flat share count. Evidence that would move them is recorded in each scenario's growth_rationale / margin_rationale and in weights_rationale.

inputs.sbc_source: not separately deducted -- SBC is already inside GAAP net income and the engine's ebitda_margin_path is a NET (post-financing, post-credit-cost) margin, not an EBITDA margin; sbc_pct_path held at 0 to avoid double-charging.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC -- net_debt is held at 0 because AXP's debt and deposits fund its ~$214B card-loan receivables book (operating funding for a lender), not leverage against the fee/network business. Base 10.5% reflects AXP's beta (~1.2-1.3, real if currently-benign consumer-credit cyclicality) against a large-cap US equity risk premium; bull 9.5% / bear 12.0% bracket credit-cycle-dependent risk.
inputs.lease_treatment: not applicable -- lease charges immaterial versus the credit/funding items driving this model (lease_cost_pct_path held at 0)
inputs.notes: Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md: AXP carries a ~$214B card-loan portfolio and net interest income ~18% of FY2025 revenue -- reported OCF/FCF is dominated by loan originations/collections and total_debt mostly funds the receivables book, so a plain owner-FCF DCF (FCF/WACC with net debt subtracted) would misstate both the flow and the bridge. Modeled instead as an earnings-based FCFE-at-cost-of-equity DCF via the standard component ENGINE (not a hand-built JSON): ebitda_margin_path is set to the projected NET margin (cash_tax_rate_path held at 0, since GAAP net income is already post-tax and post-financing) and capex_pct_path stands in for capital retained to fund loan-book/balance-sheet growth at the assumed ROE (retention_ratio = NI_growth/ROE, capped [0,0.9]; capex_pct = retention_ratio x net_margin), so nopat - capex = NI x (1 - retention) = FCFE -- exactly the mechanic NAB.AX's Drivers.json uses (see NAB.AX_Drivers.json assumptions.base.capex_rationale). Same model family as NAB.AX (FCFE-at-CoE), SOFI (earnings-based bank DCF), SRBK (residual income on tangible book), IAG.AX (FCFE-at-CoE on NEP). FY2025 net income $10,833m is the FY0 anchor; TTM (Q3-25 through Q2-26) net income is $11,446m on revenue $43,086m (~26.6% net margin), consistent with FY2026 guidance (EPS $17.30-17.90, revenue +~10%) implying FY2026 NI ~$11.86-11.9bn at ~26.1% margin -- the base-case Y1 anchor. ROE is ~33-34% TTM (management cited 36.4% for Q2-2026 annualized), far above the ~10.5% cost of equity, so most net income is genuinely distributable via buybacks even while the balance sheet keeps growing -- this matches AXP's actual capital-light buyback behavior (~$5.8bn FY2025, accelerating to $4.2bn in H1-2026 alone, ~4-5%/yr net share count decline). Terminal value uses an exit-P/E cap (16x base) rather than relying on the Gordon growth spread, since a bank/lender's terminal multiple is the more defensible anchor -- versus AXP's own current ~17.6x forward / ~18.3x TTM multiple, itself already compressed from ~25x at the Dec-2025 high per Sept-2026 press coverage, so 16x is flat-to-below today's already-de-rated multiple, not an aggressive re-rating assumption. || UPDATE 2026-11-19 (Q3-2026 10-Q): model unchanged (earnings-based FCFE at cost of equity, engine route, net debt zero). Anchors refreshed: price, share count 679.0 -> 671.6 (cover count at 15 Oct 2026 plus dilution), buyback pace to TTM, balance-sheet date to 30 Sep 2026. Revenue base corrected from the XBRL contract-revenue subset to total revenues net of interest expense -- value-neutral, see revenue_basis; read the margin figures in the paragraph above (26.1%, 26.6%) as net income over that subset. FY2026 (Y1) re-judged on nine months of actuals: revenue $58,606m (+10%; Q3 +9%), net income $9,794m including a $751m after-tax gain on the sale of the GBTG stake and a $253m after-tax restructuring charge; ex those two items 9M net income is ~$9,296m (+11%). The net one-off (+$498m) sits in equity_bridge, not in the margin path. Stub convention, unchanged and stated: Y1 is the full FY2026 flow discounted one year although ~7.4bn of it has already been distributed (9M buybacks + dividends) and the share count already reflects those buybacks; against that, every flow is discounted as if the valuation date were 31 Dec 2025, ~0.9 year early. The two offset to a net understatement of roughly 4% of value -- conservative, left as is; it unwinds when FY2026 becomes FY0. No post-Q3 management guidance document is in the research folder: the FY2026 guide on file (EPS $17.30-17.90, revenue ~+10%) dates from the Q2 call and should be re-checked against the Q3 release.
inputs.buyback_basis: TTM to 30 Sep 2026, cash flow statement: FY2025 5,814 + 9M-2026 5,805 - 9M-2025 4,915. Q3-2026 alone: $1.6bn, 4.8m shares at an average $331.37 (Q3-2026 10-Q). Pace slowed from $2.3bn in Q2 to $1.6bn in Q3; 9M payout (buybacks + common dividends) was 77% of net income available to common.
inputs.share_count_basis: 670.55m common shares outstanding at 15 Oct 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus ~1m dilutive securities (Q3 weighted average diluted 674m vs basic 673m) = 671.6m. Held flat: buybacks are what the FCFE flow pays for, so shrinking the count as well would double-count.
inputs.revenue_basis: base_revenue is FY2025 TOTAL revenues net of interest expense, $72,229m (FY2025 10-K MD&A, AXP_Annual_FY2025.txt:3549). The prior version compounded from $41,304m, which is the Metrics.csv/XBRL `revenue` column -- an ASC-606 contract-revenue subset that excludes net interest income and part of card fees. Every %-of-revenue path (net margin, retention) was rescaled by 41,304/72,229 = 0.5718 so the net-income and FCFE paths are identical; the rebase alone rebuilds the prior values to the cent (bear 134.36 / base 234.50 / bull 322.02 / weighted 231.35). Net margin is therefore now ~15%, the true figure, not ~26%.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 raised to 9.3% (was 6.0%): nine months are booked at +10%, so even a Q4 at +7% lands here; the bear case now starts from a higher, known base and the slowdown begins in FY2027. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED (4.5% then 5.0%).
bear.margin_rationale: FY2026 14.6% (was 13.72% on the same basis; net income ~$11.5bn ex the GBTG one-off = Q4 underlying down ~9% YoY as provisions start to build). The prior bear FY2026 net income of ~$10.5bn is no longer attainable with $9.3bn underlying already earned. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED: margin steps down to 12.87% in FY2027 and troughs at 12.41% as credit normalises.
bear.capex_rationale: FY2026 retention 21% (was 0): FY2026 net income now grows ~6% rather than contracting, and 21% matches the actual 9M retention of 23%. FY2027 stays at zero (net income falls ~8%), years 3-10 unchanged: ROE falls toward 20% and management preserves capital.

base.growth_rationale: Total revenues net of interest expense. FY2026 9.8% (was 10.0%): nine months actual +10%, Q3 +9%; Q4 assumed at the Q3 rate gives ~$79.3bn. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-26 version (8.7% decelerating to 5.0%) -- one quarter at 9% rather than 10% is inside the path's own deceleration and is not evidence about 2028+. What would move them: card-fee growth exiting 2026 below the guided high-teens rate, or billed-business growth (Q3 +8%) dropping under ~6%.
base.margin_rationale: NET margin on total revenues net of interest expense (cash_tax_rate_path 0: GAAP net income is post-tax, post-financing, post-credit-cost). FY2026 15.0% (was 14.93% on the same basis) = net income ~$11.9bn: 9M actual $9,794m less the net $498m GBTG/restructuring one-off = $9,296m, plus Q4 at ~+6% on Q4-2025's $2,462m. Deliberately below the simple +11% run-rate (~$12.0bn) because 9M also carried discrete tax benefits (ETR 20.9% vs 21.8%) and a model-driven credit reserve release, neither recurring. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED (15.04% rising to 15.44%; the prior 26.3%-27.0% rescaled to the full revenue base). What would move them: net write-off rate (Q3 2.1%) or 30+ day delinquency (1.2%) breaking out of the current range, or marketing/opex growth persistently above revenue growth.
base.capex_rationale: capex_pct_path is capital RETAINED to fund balance-sheet growth, not physical capex: retention = NI growth / ROE, capex_pct = retention x net margin, so NOPAT - capex = FCFE. Years 1-2 recomputed mechanically from the re-judged FY2026 net income at the same ROE assumptions as before (33% / 32%): retention 29.7% and 28.1%. Years 3-10 unchanged (rescaled to the full revenue base). Cross-check: actual 9M-2026 payout was 77% of net income (retention 23%), slightly more generous than the path.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 narrowed to 10.2% (was 11.5%): with nine months booked at $58.6bn, +10.2% already requires Q4 at ~+11%; 11.5% is no longer reachable. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED (10.5% decelerating to 5.8%): card-fee acceleration and Millennial/Gen-Z acquisition sustain a durable double-digit path.
bull.margin_rationale: FY2026 15.2% (was 15.04% on the same basis; net income ~$12.1bn ex the GBTG one-off, i.e. Q4 running at the 9M underlying pace with no give-back of the reserve release). Years 2-10 UNCHANGED (15.27% expanding to 16.13%).
bull.capex_rationale: Same retention mechanic; years 1-2 recomputed from the re-judged FY2026 net income at unchanged ROE (34% / 33.5%), years 3-10 unchanged.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25, UNCHANGED. Q3-2026 gave no reason to skew: credit improved at the margin (net write-off rate 2.1% vs 2.2%, 30+ day delinquency stable at 1.2%, CET1 10.9%), but revenue growth slipped from 10% to 9% and the headline EPS beat was a one-off asset sale. What would move the weights: delinquency above ~1.5% or a reserve build (more bear), or card-fee growth sustained in the high teens through 2027 (more bull).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
